question: Which testable research directions emerge by mixing artificial-life discovery mechanisms with graph-based materials reasoning?
archiveRule: One eligible candidate with highest mean AI-rated rubric score per target × lever cell; ties retain earlier candidate. No novelty score is added to quality.
eligibility: At least two distinct known source papers, including one ALife and one Buehler paper; each source use has a locator and explicit transfer boundary; both critics accept niche fit, have no fatal flag, and score grounding >=2. All generated mechanisms remain untested proposals.
selection: Two model-generated initial proposals deliberately seeded per cell; one feedback-guided child of each initial elite. This is a small QDAIF-inspired demonstration, not the original QDAIF implementation or an unbiased search-space coverage benchmark.
limitations: Generators, critics and revisers inherit one model family; they are separate contexts, not independent model families.
AI scores express proposal quality under this rubric, not probability of scientific success, novelty certification or empirical validation.
No proposed biological, physical or materials experiment has been executed.
Niches and source cards are human/coordinator designed; targeted initialization makes coverage easier.
Token usage was not measured and no equal-budget superiority claim is made.

papers.title: Automating the Search for Artificial Life with Foundation Models
papers.mechanism: Search rendered simulation trajectories using learned visual representations for targets, historical novelty or archive diversity.
papers.boundary: Visual and finite-horizon novelty do not establish indefinite innovation or cognition.

papers.title: Toward Artificial Open-Ended Evolution within Lenia using Quality-Diversity
papers.mechanism: Maintain many locally competitive niches; adapt learned descriptors while externally evolving Lenia seeds and rule parameters.
papers.boundary: Adaptive descriptors change the ruler; the paper does not claim theoretical open-endedness.

papers.title: From Text to Life: On the Reciprocal Relationship between Artificial Life and Large Language Models
papers.locator: LLMs as Tools for ALife; ALife for LLMs/Emergence; Collective Intelligence
papers.mechanism: A review connects model-guided variation, environmental generation and multiagent organization.
papers.boundary: A conceptual bridge does not experimentally establish living or emergently intelligent LLMs.

papers.title: SciAgents: Automating scientific discovery through multi-agent intelligent graph reasoning
papers.mechanism: Sample paths in an ontological graph and use specialized agents to generate, expand and critique materials hypotheses.
papers.boundary: Graph relations and model-proposed property improvements require independent physical validation.

papers.title: Generative retrieval-augmented ontologic graph and multi-agent strategies for interpretive large language model-based materials design
papers.locator: Results and Discussion: retrieval, ontological graphs and agent-based simulation; Materials and Methods
papers.mechanism: Ground materials reasoning in retrieved context and interpretable relation graphs; connect agent reasoning to simulation workflows.
papers.boundary: Retrieved relations are not automatically causal laws; analogies need units, mappings and executable checks.

papers.title: Quality-Diversity through AI Feedback
papers.mechanism: Use language models to generate variation and evaluate quality and diversity inside an evolutionary archive.
papers.boundary: Creative-text evidence does not establish the scientific validity of research proposals.
